ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a cuboid composite conductor, with the end faces labeled P and Q, indicating that the resistance between these two end faces is required. The figure marks the conductor length as 50 mm, and the side length of the square cross-section of the external aluminum bar as 7 mm; in the middle, along the length direction, there is a square hole, the filling material is labeled Fe, the side length of the hole is labeled 2 mm, and the surrounding material is labeled Al. Reasoning: The current passes from face P to face Q along the length direction of the bar, so the aluminum part and the iron filling part are equivalent to conducting in parallel along the same length. Given ρ_Al = 2.7×10^-8 Ω m, ρ_Fe = 1.0×10^-7 Ω m, length L = 50 mm = 0.05 m. The cross-sectional area of iron A_Fe = 2 mm × 2 mm = 4 mm^2 = 4×10^-6 m^2. The total cross-sectional area is 7 mm × 7 mm = 49 mm^2, so the effective cross-sectional area of aluminum A_Al = 49 - 4 = 45 mm^2 = 45×10^-6 m^2. Calculate separately: R_Al = ρ_Al L / A_Al = (2.7×10^-8 × 0.05)/(45×10^-6) = 3.0×10^-5 Ω = 30 μΩ. R_Fe = ρ_Fe L / A_Fe = (1.0×10^-7 × 0.05)/(4×10^-6) = 1.25×10^-3 Ω = 1250 μΩ. The parallel equivalent resistance satisfies 1/R = 1/R_Al + 1/R_Fe, so R = (30×1250)/(30+1250) μΩ = 37500/1280 μΩ = 1875/64 μΩ.

method.method_draft: Treat the aluminum part and the iron-filled square hole as two resistors in parallel along the bar length. First read from the figure that current is measured between end faces P and Q, the bar length is 50 mm, the outer square cross section is 7 mm by 7 mm, and the iron insert is a 2 mm by 2 mm square running through the bar. From the text, take resistivities rho_Al = 2.7e-8 ohm m and rho_Fe = 1.0e-7 ohm m. Compute areas A_Fe = 4 mm^2 and A_Al = 49 - 4 = 45 mm^2. Use R = rho L/A separately for the Al and Fe longitudinal paths, then combine by 1/R_eq = 1/R_Al + 1/R_Fe. Convert mm and mm^2 to SI units; this yields R_eq = 1875/64 micro-ohm.
